reviews.notes: (q+1)-partite (q+1)-uniform via edges Fin (q+1) -> Fin (q+1); Intersecting includes nonemptiness; Nonisolated gives exactly q+1 nonisolated vertices per part; HasCoverNumber (q+1); all sufficiently large primes. Matches docs/162.md.

reviews.reviewer: Claude (Anthropic), directed by Caleb J. Westfall
reviews.notes: SubquadraticMemory: universal c, o(d^2) memory, 0<eps<=1/10, success >= 2/3 uniformly or for every signal. FixedQuadraticMemory: for every A>0 a constant c_A. Matches docs/140.md.

reviews.reviewer: Claude (Anthropic), directed by Caleb J. Westfall
reviews.notes: 0<beta<1; Poincare event and discrete gap >= 1/(Cn) each with probability tending to 1. discreteGap is an sInf of a set bounded below by 0. Matches docs/227.md.

reviews.reviewer: Claude (Anthropic), directed by Caleb J. Westfall
reviews.notes: 0<=beta<1/2, 0<eps<1/2, eta>0; probability of ratio > 1+eta tends to 0; denominator eventually positive is stated, which guards the sInf/division junk values. Matches docs/227.md.

reviews.reviewer: Claude (Anthropic), directed by Caleb J. Westfall
reviews.notes: Matches docs/237.md up to wording: the corridor is |x| <= h(log h)^2, a full width of 2h(log h)^2, and degenerates to |x| <= 0 at h = 1. Logically, the five other clauses follow from Summable firstLengthWeight (weights are nonnegative and length >= 1; subtypes and constant multiples of summable families are summable), so the corridor clauses add no content. Not an error; not yet kernel-certified (needs Mathlib).

reviews.reviewer: Claude (Anthropic), directed by Caleb J. Westfall
reviews.notes: freeEnergy is limUnder; the theorem asserts Tendsto to it, i.e. the limit exists, for every vertex, direction and real force parameter. rho = (sqrt(2+sqrt 2))^-1 is the critical honeycomb activity. Matches docs/237.md.

reviews.reviewer: Claude (Anthropic), directed by Caleb J. Westfall
reviews.notes: Integrability of |phi'|^s for 4/3<s<4 over simply connected domains with nontrivial spherical boundary; |f'|^t for -2<t<2/3; B_S(-2)=1 via an EReal limsup (no junk value). Matches docs/072.md. Note: this is a statement of Brennan's conjecture; the result's correctness is outside this review.

reviews.reviewer: Claude (Anthropic), directed by Caleb J. Westfall
reviews.notes: Real liminf/limsup of the prescribed slope are protected by the explicit upper bound v k <= 1 + k^(2^(k-1)) and the stated chain liminf <= limsup. Matches docs/025.md.

reviews.reviewer: Claude (Anthropic), directed by Caleb J. Westfall
reviews.notes: Matches docs/263.md as written. IteratedLimits uses real-valued limsup/liminf over Z; in Lean these take a junk value (0) when the sequence is unbounded, so the proved statement (limit a > 0) implies that for all large m the ionization energy I_m(Z) is bounded in Z. An expert should confirm this consequence is intended and matches the paper's convention. PAPER CROSS-CHECK 2026-11-08: preprints/Generalized-ionization-energies-for-full-Coulomb-atoms-September-24-2026/paper.pdf, Theorem 1.1 eqs (1.3)-(1.5), Section 6.3. Paper explicitly discusses potentially infinite inner limits and derives their eventual behavior from the joint limit; it does not assume fixed-m convergence. Thus the real-limsup issue alone is NOT a certified discrepancy; precise formal handling of exceptional m still needs a Mathlib-specific proof and expert review.

reviews.reviewer: Claude (Anthropic), directed by Caleb J. Westfall
reviews.notes: Matches docs/024.md. The zero case assumes no totient d with k*d < ell(d). If that hypothesis fails for every k >= 1 the theorem is vacuous; whether it ever holds was not determined. A is a limUnder; the conclusion A = 0 is meaningful only if the approximants converge, which holds trivially if they vanish. PAPER CROSS-CHECK 2026-11-08: preprints/An-asymptotic-formula-for-the-number-of-totients-September-25-2026/An-asymptotic-formula-for-the-number-of-totients-September-25-2026.pdf, Theorem 2.2 (thm:companion), alternative (ii). The paper explicitly states the exact same no-seed implication N_k(x)=0 for every x>0 and A(f_k;s)=0 for 0<=s<1; alternative (i) is asserted for k=1,2. Whether alternative (ii) holds for any k>2 remains unresolved in this review; no mismatch certified.
